title: The Diffusion and Reach of (Mis)Information on Facebook During the U.S. 2020 Election
screen_reason: Full-platform Meta data on every post published by U.S.-based adult accounts and re-shared at least once, 1 July 2020 – 1 February 2021. Posts re-shared >=100 times ('large trees', ~12.1 M) are partitioned into ~114,000 rated false by third-party fact-checkers, ~2,000 rated true and ~12 M unlabeled — an exact part/whole share with a stated denominator. Eligible on the CONTENT/SHARING criterion.

estimates.measure_type: % of Facebook posts re-shared 100+ times by U.S. adults that were rated false by third-party fact-checkers
estimates.value_raw: N ~ 114,000 trees labeled as misinformation out of ~12.1 M large trees (114,000/12,100,000 = 0.94%); the remainder are ~2,000 rated true and ~12 M unlabeled
estimates.denominator: ~12.1 million 'large trees' — posts (text, URLs, images, videos) published publicly or privately by U.S.-based adult accounts and re-shared at least 100 times, i.e. 1.2% of the ~1.02 billion posts re-shared at least once
estimates.definition: Root post content rated 'false' by a third-party fact-checker in Meta's 3PFC network, or content matched by Meta to a post carrying that rating
estimates.misinfo_def: "We classify as 'misinformation' content (including text, URLs, images, and videos) that was rated "false" by 3PFCs, a network that includes organizations such as Snopes, Reuters, The Washington Post, Fact Checker, FactCheck.org, and PolitiFact, among others."
estimates.source_quote: In total, N ∼ 114, 000 trees are labeled as misinformation.
estimates.page_loc: Data and Measures, pp. 1132–1133; denominator from p. 1130 and the Figure 1 caption, p. 1131
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Meta's third-party fact-checking (3PFC) network — Snopes, Reuters, The Washington Post Fact Checker, FactCheck.org, PolitiFact and others — rated content 'false'; Meta then propagated the label to matching content (e.g. other posts with the same URL). The authors stress that they do not know why some content was fact-checked and other content not, that Facebook surfaces candidate content to fact-checkers using signals likely correlated with reach, and that posts from politicians' Pages containing the politicians' own claims were ineligible for fact-checking. No inter-rater reliability is reported.
estimates.moderator_quote: The data for this article draw from all U.S.-based monthly active adult users, and track exposures to and re-sharing of all posts published (publicly or privately) on the platform from July 1, 2020, to February 1, 2021. … To protect privacy, we only have access to tree-level data for the posts that were shared (both privately and publicly) at least k = 100 times by U.S. users (1.2 percent or 12.1 M posts).
estimates.notes: CONSTRUCT CALL (borderline=true): the denominator is defined by re-sharing (posts re-shared >=100 times), so under the denominator-sets-the-construct rule this is SHARING with sharing_subtype=content_share ('% of shared items that are misinfo'). An adjudicator could reasonably code it CONTENT instead, since the units counted are distinct posts rather than share events and the number reads as a content-prevalence statistic. Flagged rather than silently chosen. VALUE: 0.94% is a part/whole from the two counts the paper states, but both are the authors' own rounded approximations (N ~ 114,000; 12.1 M), so the third digit is not meaningful — treat as ~0.9%. The paper never states this percentage itself. DENOMINATOR: restricted to the >=100-reshare subset (1.2% of all re-shared posts), which is a rank-truncated selection, hence denom_selection=curated; these large trees carry 54.5% of all views. The share among ALL ~1.02 B re-shared posts is not derivable, and the authors say plainly they are 'likely underestimating the prevalence of misinformation on the platform'. Data window straddles 2020–2021; year set to 2020 (seven of eight months). topic='other' because the corpus is all platform content, not topic-restricted (political posts are analysed as a separate subset).

missed_or_uncertain: (1) CONCENTRATION not extractable under R1: the paper twice states the group but never a numeric share — 'less than 1 percent of users generate most of the content labeled by 3PFCs as "false"' and 'we estimate that ∼ 1 percent of users account for most misinformation re-shares'. conc_group_pct would be 1 but conc_share_pct is only 'most', so the row would be unusable; the underlying estimate lives in online supplement S5.15, not in this text. This is the single most important thing an adjudicator might want to chase in the supplement. (2) A tree-level concentration figure IS given — 1.2% of re-shared posts (the large trees) accumulate 54.5% of all views — but the unit is posts, not users or sources, so it does not fit conc_unit (user|source) and it is not misinformation-specific. Not extracted. (3) Reach-threshold shares are within-misinformation distributions, not prevalence: for misinformation, 10.6% of Page posts and 2.7% of user posts reach 100K views, 1.4% and 0.4% reach 1 M views; overall 24.4% of Page posts vs 8.2% of user trees reach 100K views, 1.8% vs 1.9% reach 1 M. No row. (4) Composition within the misinformation set: users initiated 89% of the ~114,000 'false' trees, and only ~16,000 of them also carry the 'untrustworthy source' label (users account for 3% of those). A source-composition figure, not a falsity share, so not kept even under R3. (5) Average tree sizes (misinformation 682, political 697, all 919) and the period-by-period declines (~30% all large trees, ~70% political, ~90% misinformation, July–December) are volumes and structural statistics, not shares with a denominator. (6) Figure 4D reports misinformation views falling from ~50 M/day to near zero before Election Day — read off a figure, no denominator, not extracted.

rob.design: Observational full-platform data from Meta covering all U.S.-based monthly active adult users, 1 July 2020 – 1 February 2021; no sampling and no response rate. Universe: ~1.02 billion posts re-shared at least once; tree-level analysis restricted for privacy to the 1.2% (12.1 M) re-shared >=100 times, which hold 54.5% of all views. Diffusion edges defined by an actual click on the re-share button (misses copy-paste re-posting). Misinformation identified solely by third-party fact-checker 'false' ratings propagated to matching content; no reliability statistics for those ratings, selection into fact-checking unknown and likely correlated with reach, politicians' own claims exempt from fact-checking. Authors list five limitations, including no access to the underlying social network and no ability to generalise to unlabeled misinformation.
rob.item6_quote: We classify as 'misinformation' content (including text, URLs, images, and videos) that was rated "false" by 3PFCs, a network that includes organizations such as Snopes, Reuters, The Washington Post, Fact Checker, FactCheck.org, and PolitiFact, among others.
rob.item10_quote: Of all the posts that were re-shared at least once (N ∼ 1.02 B), only 1.2 percent (or 12.1 M) reached the k >= 100 re-shares threshold. … In total, N ∼ 114, 000 trees are labeled as misinformation.
